title: Intervenable Concept Dynamics for Video Activity Forecasting
abstract: arXiv:2611.00020v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Concept bottleneck models route predictions through human-understandable concepts, making their intermediate states inspectable and editable. Extending this model family to forecasting requires modeling how concept activations evolve over time as objects, actions, and their interactions change, yet existing CBMs ground concepts only in observed inputs and do not forecast their future evolution. We study this problem using videos of ongoing activities and forecast future activities through a named-concept state. We propose TRACE-CBM (Temporal Relational Activity Concept Evolution), which first refines observed concept activations with sparse spatio-temporal graphs. It then recursively predicts future concept states, conditioning each transition on the prior activity distribution, and decodes both observed and predicted states with a shared activity classifier. translated_title: 用于视频活动预测的可干预概念动力学
translated_abstract: 概念瓶颈模型通过人类可理解的概念来传递预测，使其中间状态可检查、可编辑。将这一模型家族扩展到预测任务，需要建模概念激活如何随着物体、动作及其交互的变化而随时间演化，然而现有的概念瓶颈模型仅将概念建立在观测输入上，并不预测其未来演化。我们利用正在进行的活动视频来研究这一问题，并通过命名概念状态来预测未来活动。我们提出了TRACE-CBM（时序关系活动概念演化）方法，该方法首先利用稀疏时空图对观测到的概念激活进行细化，随后递归地预测未来概念状态，每次状态转移均以先验活动分布为条件，并使用共享的活动分类器对观测状态和预测状态进行解码。在推理阶段，该模型支持编辑概念值与活动……
tldr: 本文提出TRACE-CBM框架，利用稀疏时空图细化观测概念激活并递归预测未来概念状态演化，首次实现了基于可编辑命名概念状态的视频未来活动预测。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes TRACE-CBM, which refines observed concept activations with sparse spatio-temporal graphs and recursively forecasts future concept states, enabling intervenable video activity prediction through named-concept dynamics.
